name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
moat_justification: Intermodal scale and rail partnerships built since 1990 plus sticky dedicated contracts give real network and retention advantages, but JBHT owns no railroad, pricing power is cyclical, and truckload/brokerage are near-commodity.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.5%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 8.97 vs 3-yr median 5.37 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality intermodal leader, moat 6/10, but priced for a supercycle — weighted IRR 7.2%, IV@15 $85.88 vs $230.00 price; clears 15% only at or below $85.88.
moat_for: Intermodal leadership — 20%-plus share, network density cuts empty moves and improves asset turns
Class I rail partnerships since 1990 (BNSF West, Norfolk Southern East) hard to replicate at scale
Dedicated Contract Services stickiness — contract-based, embedded, ~96% retention
Scale cost-to-serve program, 360 platform, and buybacks shrinking shares 2.5%/yr
moat_against: Owns no railroad — line-haul depends on Class I service and pricing
Freight pricing power is cyclical; highway capacity loosening compresses intermodal pricing
Hub Group, Schneider, Knight-Swift and STG compete in intermodal; truckload/brokerage near-commodity
Purchased transportation, driver, insurance and claims cost inflation outside its control
